text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nine MPs from western Nyanza province appeal for food aid because of a drought, arguing it is needed to save their people from death by starvation.
- A new row breaks out in opposition FORD-Kenya as members disown a statement by six FORD-Kenya leaders on Friday that a quest for a single opposition presidential candidate was dead.
- Eight men, seven of them Ugandans, are sentenced to death in two separate courts for robbery with violence and attempted robbery.

- An 18-year-old girl allegedly raped by 11 men last weekend is still in hospital in central Rachuonyo district and the prosecution opposes release of the men on bail following threats from the victim's family.
- President Daniel arap Moi appeals to the Tugen, Pokot, Marakwet and Turkana communities in north Kenya to stop cattle rustling, saying it impedes development.

- Villagers and opposition leaders in western Kakamega district accuse the police of harassing the family of the late Solomon Muruli, a University of Nairobi student leader who died in suspicious circumstances last month.
- East African Co-operation between Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda marks its first anniversary.
- The decision by six FORD-Kenya "young Turks" to form a pressure group for constitutional reform ahead of the General Election is condemned by both opposition and ruling party leaders.

- A meeting of the Bureau of the Conference of African Industry ministers hears that Africa could be marginalised in trade and industry owing to its debt burden, deterioration of terms of trade and reduction of devlopment aid.
